bull.b: Growth across several ophthalmic franchises reduces reliance on a single product and indicates expanding commercial adoption. Rising prescriptions, ordering accounts, surgical use, and branded dry-eye share provide multiple durable drivers for revenue growth over the coming quarters.

TYRVAYA adds an FDA-approved, drop-free dry-eye therapy to Harrow’s existing VEVYE franchise and brings roughly 40 experienced commercial personnel. The broader portfolio and shared infrastructure could strengthen market coverage and support incremental growth after integration.

bull.t: Strong Product Economics And Cash Generation
bull.b: High gross margins suggest attractive product economics, while the shift to positive operating and free cash flow improves internal funding capacity. Sustained cash generation could support commercialization, integration spending, and eventual deleveraging if operating momentum continues.

bear.t: Higher Leverage And Thin Equity Cushion
bear.b: Greater debt alongside a sharply reduced equity base increases refinancing and dilution risk and leaves less room to absorb weaker operating results. The company therefore depends more heavily on sustained cash generation and successful execution to preserve financial flexibility.

bear.t: Weak Profitability And Rising Operating Costs
bear.b: Strong revenue and gross margins have not yet translated into consistent earnings because operating costs remain elevated and losses widened. Negative quarterly adjusted EBITDA, plus planned post-acquisition SG&A increases, could delay durable profitability and pressure cash resources.

Meeting annual guidance requires a substantial second-half acceleration across product launches, channel normalization, sales-force productivity, and integration. Reimbursement loss in ASC settings adds a continuing access headwind that could constrain IHEEZO adoption and revenue conversion.
